Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM

Source: R/zinbreg.R
zinbreg.Rd

Fits the ZINB model $$P(Y_i = 0) = \pi_i + (1 - \pi_i) f_{NB}(0; \mu_i, \theta), \quad P(Y_i = y) = (1 - \pi_i) f_{NB}(y; \mu_i, \theta),\ y \ge 1,$$ with \(\log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) and \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\), by an EM algorithm. The E-step computes the posterior probability \(\tau_i\) that observation \(i\) is a structural zero; the M-step fits a logistic regression with fractional response \(\tau_i\) by IRLS (zero part) and a weighted NB regression with prior weights \(1 - \tau_i\) by nbreg()'s IRLS / Newton-Raphson algorithm (count part). Standard errors come from the observed information of the observed-data log-likelihood in \((\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\). The results agree with pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin").

Usage

zinbreg(
  formula,
  data,
  subset,
  na.action,
  weights,
  offset,
  control = zinbreg_control(...),
  model = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: count-model covariates before |, zero-model covariates after it. Without | the same covariates are used in both parts. Offsets (in the formula or via offset) apply to the count part only.

data

A data frame containing the variables in the model.

subset

Optional expression selecting the rows of data to use.

na.action

How to handle missing values (default from getOption("na.action")).

weights

Optional non-negative prior weights \(a_i\).

offset

Optional offset vector (added to the linear predictor).

control

A list from zinbreg_control().

model

Logical; keep the model frame in the result?

...

Arguments passed to zinbreg_control() when control is not given.

Value

An object of class "zinbreg", a list with components including coefficients (a list with count and zero), vcov (covariance of all count and zero coefficients), vcov_full (also including log(theta)), theta, SE.logtheta, SE.theta, loglik, iter, converged, loglik_trace, fitted.values (\((1-\pi_i)\mu_i\)), mu, pi, y, x, z, weights, offset, df.residual and call.

See also

nbreg(), summary.zinbreg(), predict.zinbreg()

Examples

data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
fit <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
               data = bioChemists)
summary(fit)
#>

#> zinbreg(formula = art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
